knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Zones, sequence, spot test, runoff and the pedestrian edge are planned before the first pass, so the controls are in place when the water is used.
Damage found in a spot test is a stop trigger. The test is recorded and the method is changed or referred, rather than widened.
Runoff must be contained or routed, and no wastewater is released to stormwater [VIC-EPA-980]. The local rules are checked first.

practicalCriteria: Produces a site plan for a sample building that marks the spray, exclusion, equipment, runoff and access zones, and the surface sequence, checked by the assessor against a checklist.
Completes a spot-test log for two sample materials, recording location, method, result and time, and states the stop decision for a sample damage result.
Briefs a sample team, naming the spotter, the stop authority and the runoff route, and the briefing is recorded and signed.
passRule: Assessor review of the site plan, spot-test log and briefing record for the sample site, with all three practical criteria met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Site plan with the zones and sequence
Team briefing record with each person's role
stopWorkCriteria: A pedestrian enters the exclusion zone and there is no spotter
Runoff reaches a stormwater drain or waterway without containment
A spot test shows damage and the wider method continues
Electrical equipment is in the spray or a cord crosses the water path
